body:
An extra eventloop sounds like a good idea... Whould you mind creating one?

Sent from my iPhone. Excuse any typos....

Am 30.09.2012 um 08:59 schrieb Jestan Nirojan notifications@github.com:

> Since com.sun.nio.sctp.SctpChannel is a InterruptibleChannel, OioEventLoop's thread.interrupt() usage (to switch read/write in single threaded event loop) closes the channel prematurely.
> 
> java.nio.channels.ClosedByInterruptException
> java.nio.channels.ClosedByInterruptException
> at java.nio.channels.spi.AbstractInterruptibleChannel.end(AbstractInterruptibleChannel.java:202)
> at sun.nio.ch.SctpChannelImpl.receive(SctpChannelImpl.java:772)
> at sun.nio.ch.SctpChannelImpl.receive(SctpChannelImpl.java:730)
> at io.netty.channel.socket.oio.OioSctpChannel.doReadMessages(OioSctpChannel.java:117)
> at io.netty.channel.socket.oio.AbstractOioMessageChannel$OioMessageUnsafe.read(AbstractOioMessageChannel.java:45)
> at io.netty.channel.socket.oio.OioEventLoop.run(OioEventLoop.java:81)
> at io.netty.channel.SingleThreadEventExecutor$1.run(SingleThreadEventExecutor.java:80)
> at java.lang.Thread.run(Thread.java:722)
> 
> So I did following change in OioEventLoop to get it working. This change was merged into the master without review (netty/netty#619) :-) .
> 
> OioEventLoop: before OioSctpChannel
> 
> protected void wakeup(boolean inEventLoop) {
>     interruptThread();
> }
> OioEventLoop: change after OioSctpChannel pull request
> 
> protected void wakeup(boolean inEventLoop) {
>     if (!inEventLoop && isShutdown()) {
>         interruptThread();
>     }
> }
> Now problem is, OioSctpChannel's write() does not work properly sometime because, the event loop thread is blocked on ch.unsafe().read(); foreever without processing task queue.
> 
> Can we come up with a separate EventLoop for blocking InterruptibleChannels or is there any other way to solve this issue?
> 
> Please note that, I could not reproduce this issue with OioSocketChannel or even in OioSctpEchoClient/Server :)
> 
> —
> Reply to this email directly or view it on GitHub.

I am just wondering how many threads we need to implement a EventLoop for blocking InterruptibleChannel?
3 threads? reader, writer, channel operation :-( .

Sounds correct..

Am 01.10.2012 um 10:38 schrieb Jestan Nirojan notifications@github.com:

> I am just wondering how many threads we need to implement a EventLoop for blocking InterruptibleChannel?
> 3 threads? reader, writer, channel opertion :-( .
> 
> —
> Reply to this email directly or view it on GitHub.

@jestan, is there any way to set read timeout for a blocking read?  I saw someone implemented read/write timeout using a temporary selector.  That is, you can turn on non-blocking mode on the channel, acquire a selector from a selector pool, register a single channel to the selector, and select with timeout for reads, and then handle timeout.  Not sure this is going to be perfoming well though.  I guess we should give it a shot though.

@trustin @normanmaurer  I could not find a way to set the read timeout, so tried with selector approach. Currently I am using three selectors (read, write and connect) which I don't like, is there any way to use a single selector without additional if else checks. Could you please explain, how to use temporary selector and selector pool here?

@jestan, Your code looks OK.  Was it (6aba1648c457163fd250b12455d3288b1bbd8b92) merged? If not, please do so.  Your code take advantage of selector pooling though.  That is, you can create a queue/stack of selectors and get the selector from there and add it back there instead of closing it.  The queue will have to be thread safe. For increased concurrency, you might want to create multiple queues so that the multiple queues handle different threads, just like we do with NIO workers.
